scope: Desktop browser automation with iPhone identification; real DOM activation, injected FileList and byte-preserving uploads.
limitations: Playwright supplies synthetic files and bypasses iOS PHPicker, Photos export, HEIC/HEVC decoding and photo-library conversion.
This does not reproduce or prove a fix for the physical iPhone white-circle problem.
Synthetic media bytes are transfer fixtures, not playable camera media.
checks: iPhone has separate media and file controls; the modal installs the bundled shortcut and gives two action-only steps including Current format. Closing restores focus and the modal fits the viewport.
Normal file input remains unrestricted and multiple; iOS picker test stays collapsed until explicitly opened.
A real click opens the chooser; no change remains pending after focus/visibility events. Empty selection creates no upload and never asserts a user cancellation or an upload failure.
Multi-file HEIC and QuickTime payloads survive synchronous FileList copying and immediate input reset; both original byte sequences download unchanged.
Selecting the same file again triggers a new complete upload after input reset.
Visible single native input receives a trusted direct click without HTMLElement.click, accept or capture; original File uploads with no Blob.arrayBuffer, canvas or image decoding.
Picker diagnostics retain only the latest 32 RAM events and at most two attempts; no filename, token, URL or raw MIME is included. Repeated empty selections send no file request.
Android retains the normal multiple-file picker and has no visible iOS test control.
A stored failed task opens the single-file retry picker, then a new upload restores multiple selection and completes both files.
